question: Should OpenClaw expose a post-subagent-completion/pre-announcement hook as a typed plugin lifecycle hook, a broader generic delivery boundary, or keep completion processing observation-only?
rationale: The choice controls public plugin API names, payload sensitivity, hook ordering, delivery-failure semantics, and whether plugins may modify or suppress user-visible completion output.

options.title: Design a generic completion/delivery boundary
options.body: Define one typed contract that covers subagent completion inspection, safe output filtering, delivery failure visibility, and announcement mutation without adding narrow one-off hooks.

options.title: Add a narrow subagent completion hook
options.body: Expose only the requested subagent-specific post-completion/pre-announcement hook with strict payload and return limits, leaving broader delivery guards for later.

options.title: Keep hooks observation-only
options.body: Do not let plugins modify completion announcements; instead improve observability and channel delivery failure reporting through existing lifecycle events.

recommendation.title: Design a generic completion/delivery boundary
recommendation.body: Define one typed contract that covers subagent completion inspection, safe output filtering, delivery failure visibility, and announcement mutation without adding narrow one-off hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent subagent lifecycle refactors and the maintainer review closing the overlapping guard-hook PR make this the clearest available design-routing signal.
